title: ZIEHL-ABEGG SE | LinkedIn
content:
Overview:
ZIEHL-ABEGG (Künzelsau, Germany) is one of the leading global companies in the field of ventilation, control and drive technology. In the 1950s, ZIEHL-ABEGG established the basis for modern fan drives: external rotor motors which even today are still seen as state-of-the-art worldwide. Another area of business is electric motors which provide the power, for example, for elevators or medical applications (computer tomography equipment). ZIEHL-ABEGG employs 3,000 personnel in its production plants in Southern Germany. The company has a global workforce of 5,800 spread between 17 production plants, 30 companies and 114 sales locations. The products, approx. 30,000 in all, are sold in more than 100 countries. Turnover in 2025 totaled more than one billion euros. Emil Ziehl founded the company in Berlin in 1910 as a manufacturer of electric motors. After the Second World War the company’s headquarters were relocated to Southern Germany. ZIEHL-ABEGG SE is not a listed company but instead is family-owned. We make the world livable. title: Ziehl-Abegg breaks the one-billion-euro barrier
content: On the website for your region you will find information on the products relevant to you, contact details and news. Ziehl-Abegg (Künzelsau, Germany) has released preliminary business figures for 2025: for the first time in the company’s 116-year history, revenue exceeded one billion euros (previous year: EUR 893 million). With year-on-year growth of more than 12 percent, the globally active manufacturer of fans and drive motors reaches a major milestone. “This milestone is more than just a number to us – it represents the performance, commitment and cohesion of our teams around the world,” says Joachim Ley, CEO of Ziehl-Abegg. That makes this result all the more impressive and demonstrates what we are capable of as a company.” As is tradition, Ziehl-Abegg does not disclose earnings. A key driver of growth was strong international business: the United States is now Ziehl-Abegg’s most important foreign market, accounting for well over 20 percent of total revenue.
